To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a prototype head-mounted display was built that allows the user to change the focal distance of one eye from infinity to the close viewing range of the eye.

we have built and evaluated a see-through HDM with an active optical element that can change the focal distance of an image presented to the eye, that we have demonstrated the capability of the HMD to present images at different focal distances, and that we have shown that the HMD can be used to measure the accommodation response of a viewer to different images.

we have designed, constructed, and tested a prototype of an optical see-through head-mounted display with an addressable focal plane that allows for a variable focal distance from infinity to the viewer’s near point.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a novel HMD that provides a correct presentation of the coupled accommodation-convergence cues.
the design and implementation of a see-through HMT with an active optical element that allows the user to select the focal distance for each eye independently.
the design and implementation of a see-through HDM with addressable focal plane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this prototype is able to present the accommodation and convergence cues correctly to the viewer and that it does so with no adverse effects.
this prototype is the first of its kind, and that it is a significant advance towards the goal of a truly comfortable and effective see-through HMD for augmented reality applications.

the prototype was able to provide a wide range of focal distances and that the accommodation response of the viewer was able to match the displayed focal distance, thus providing a more natural viewing experience for the viewer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prototype is able to present a range of focal distances that can be controlled by the viewer, thus reducing the visual fatigue and diplopic vision.

a liquid lens-based see-through HMD, with the ability to address focal distances from infinity to the eye's near point, is feasible and could be an important tool in improving the performance of the HMDs.

we have developed a prototype HMD that can address accommodation and convergence, which is a step toward the ultimate goal of building an optical see-through HMD that can provide a natural visual experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the liquid lens can be used to provide a focal distance that matches the accommodation of the viewer and thus can reduce or eliminate visual fatigue and depth perception errors caused by the fixed focal distance of existing see-through HMDs.
the proposed design provides a means to control the accommodation response of a viewer and can be used to improve the performance of existing HMDs.

a see-through HDM with an addressable focal plane can be implemented with a relatively simple and inexpensive liquid lens, and that the accommodation cues can be controlled by varying the focal plane of the HMD. Proc. SPI
